title: tool-calling: improve execution ergonomics for parallel multi-tool calls, result injection and retries
author: Maya Thompson
release_notes:
- Add parallel tool execution orchestration with deterministic ordering and configurable concurrency.
- Add tool result injection hooks and structured output improvements for OpenAI compatibility layer.
- Add retry/backoff policy for failed tool invocations and idempotency markers.
- Streaming stability fixes when injecting tool outputs mid-stream.
- SDK updates (python/typescript) for new tool-calling params.
description:
Context: We've seen several production integrations where multi-tool flows (e.g., user intent -> call 2–4 independent external tools in parallel -> aggregate results into a final response) are jittery: retries cause duplicated injections, streaming breaks when a tool returns after the LM has continued streaming, and SDK ergonomics require manual orchestration. This PR implements a runtime + API surface to make multi-tool and parallel tool calls robust and ergonomically easy for customers.

What this PR does: Adds a parallel tool execution orchestrator that: (1) accepts multiple tool descriptors and runs compatible tool invocations concurrently with a configurable max_concurrency; (2) attaches idempotency tokens and invocation ids so retries are deduplicated; (3) supports a deterministic merge policy (first-completed / priority list / ordered-aggregate) configurable per-call; (4) exposes a tool_result_injection point that safely injects structured tool outputs into the model context (supports streaming and non-streaming responses); (5) provides automatic retry/backoff with a pluggable policy and a configurable max_attempts. Also includes OpenAI-compat layer updates so existing tool_caller fields are accepted and mapped to our new orchestration metadata, plus SDK helpers for python/ts to call the new APIs.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (ENG-1428) - [x] Runtime orchestration and scheduler changes - [x] Tool invocation idempotency and retry policy - [x] Streaming stable injection tests - [x] OpenAI compatibility shims - [x] SDK convenience methods + tests - [x] E2E test matrix updated - [x] Docs + changelog

Risk/migration notes: Default behaviour is backward-compatible: single-tool calls and serial tool execution keep existing semantics. New params are opt-in (max_concurrency, merge_policy, retry_policy). OpenAI-compat layer accepts both old and new shapes; when both shapes present we prefer explicit new fields. We recommend customers adopt idempotency tokens for critical side-effects.

Related: ENG-1428 (design), ENG-1435 (e2e failures observed in staging), SUP-814 (customer case that motivated retries).

review_comments: Arjun Patel (review): Can we guarantee ordering when users choose ordered-aggregate? Need explicit deterministic behavior in doc. — reply by @Maya: Ordered-aggregate preserves the provided ordering in the request; added unit tests and a note in the API docs.

Lina Gomez (request changes): The retry policy currently retries non-idempotent tool calls by default. We should default to no-retry for non-idempotent tools and require opt-in. — reply by @Maya: Switched default to no-retry for tools marked non_idempotent; added idempotency_token field and updated SDK to surface it.
Evan Cho (nit): Minor naming nit: `ToolInvocation` vs `ToolCall`. Prefer `ToolInvocation` for clarity. — reply by @Maya: Renamed API message to ToolInvocation across the surface. Thanks.

QA (comment): e2e scenario 'parallel-aggregate-fallback' flaked once in CI due to timing; added additional retries and a flake guard. — reply by @Maya: Increased timeouts and added deterministic seeding for the test harness.

Security (comment): Ensure invocation-id is randomly generated and not user-provided to avoid collisions when recommended. — reply by @Maya: Invocation-id is generated by clients or SDKs; server validates format and enforces TTL. Documented best-practice: SDKs generate RFC4122 v4 by default.
Prod (approval): Verified staging runs with SUP-814 replay, observed no duplicate side-effects after changes. Approving to merge. — approval by @Arjun

notes_for_release: Opt-in feature for multi-tool parallel execution. Recommend customers update SDKs to get idempotency helpers. No breaking changes for default single-tool flows.
e2e_validation: E2E matrix (small/medium/large payloads) passed in staging; SUP-814 replay verified; observed median latency improvement for multi-tool flows when max_concurrency > 1 and merge_policy=ordered-aggregate.
tests_added: e2e multi-tool flows, unit tests for dedupe store, streaming injection unit tests, sdk tests (python/ts)
notes: Follow-up items: (1) add configurable per-tenant retry budget, (2) expose metrics for per-invocation latency breakdown, (3) consider a 'safe-merge' policy that scans tool outputs for conflicts before injection.
